title: Senior Manager Accountability
summary: How senior manager accountability regimes allocate individual responsibility, how the board uses them to drive conduct, and what reasonable steps look like in practice.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How senior manager accountability regimes allocate individual responsibility, how the board uses them to drive conduct, and what reasonable steps look like in practice.
Learning Objectives: Explain the core features of senior manager accountability regimes
Evaluate statements of responsibilities, mapping and conduct rule training
Apply the reasonable steps standard to board and executive oversight
Syllabus: Statements of responsibilities and responsibilities maps
Conduct rules for directors, senior managers and staff
Certification and annual fitness and propriety assessment
Evidencing reasonable steps and handling accountability gaps
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors and members of board risk, audit, remuneration and nomination committees
Executive directors and senior managers accountable for conduct, people and customer outcomes
Heads of HR, compliance and company secretarial supporting board oversight of culture
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No specialist background in HR or behavioural science is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
FSB, Guidance on Supervisory Interaction with Financial Institutions on Risk Culture (2014)
FSB, Supplementary Guidance to the FSB Principles and Standards on Sound Compensation Practices (2018)
Group of Thirty, Banking Conduct and Culture: A Call for Sustained and Comprehensive Reform (2015)
